findings.title: Extremely short reporting window
findings.deviation: Requires reporting of Privacy Events within 12 hours of discovery, which is significantly more stringent than the industry standard (typically 24-72 hours).
findings.impact: The subcontractor may be unable to meet this timeline, leading to a technical breach and potential liability for AtliQ under the upstream Harrington agreement.
findings.quote: Subcontractor shall report to Business Associate any Privacy Event within twelve (12) hours of discovery.
findings.counterPosition: Increase the reporting window to 48 or 72 hours.

findings.title: Uncapped data liability
findings.deviation: The BAA is silent on liability caps for data incidents, implying unlimited liability for the subcontractor.
findings.impact: Exposes the subcontractor to unlimited financial risk, which is inconsistent with AtliQ's mirror-test standard of capping data-related liability.
findings.quote: The Agreement is silent on liability limits.
findings.counterPosition: Apply a liability cap (e.g., 1x fees) or a specific super-cap for data breaches (e.g., 2x fees).

findings.title: Mandatory prior client approval
findings.deviation: Subcontractor is restricted from performing work until Harrington Health provides prior written approval.
findings.impact: Gives the end client veto power over AtliQ's staffing choices and may delay the start of services.
findings.quote: only after Harrington's prior written approval of Subcontractor has been obtained.
findings.counterPosition: Require only that the subcontractor meets specified qualifications or that AtliQ provides notification, rather than requiring affirmative client consent.

fine.note: The US-only access requirement (3.1) is a mandatory flow-down from the Harrington Upstream BAA.
The 10-day timeline for return or destruction of PHI (5.1) is standard and acceptable.
Restrictions on de-identification (3.3) are appropriate for ensuring compliance with client data handling rules.
